layer: dettivo-language::raw with the dictionary as whole-word replacements
note: Recorded by crates/dettivo-language/tests/dictionary_eval.rs, which fails when a figure or a row moves. Linux has no dictionary corrector yet: the raw layer's whole-word replacement is the nearest thing to the macOS `exact` strategy, and it differs from it in two ways the row lists show. It matches a dictionary word only when the transcript spells it the same (macOS `exact` also joins spaced and re-cased spellings: `super whisper` to `Superwhisper`), and it replaces a dictionary word wherever the word appears, including a common word (`linear`, `sparkle`), which macOS refuses through its common-word list. A URL, a path or another protected token is left alone on both sides: the raw layer's protected tokens (`[dictation] protect_tokens`, ADR 0023) keep `https://linear.app/...` whole, so `negative-url-001` passes. The macOS `hybrid` strategy (the shipped corrector, fn-71 there) is the bar; porting it is a spec of its own, and this report is the figure it has to move.
